summary: Multnomah County, Mt Hood NF: a 1913 tent and alidade platform on Palmer Peak, listed as an emergency lookout in 1946, gone or removed.

facts.design: tent and alidade platform set up in 1913; firelookout.com calls it a platform and camp
facts.status_note: firetower.org and firelookout.com say the 1913 platform is gone; the Oregon lookout history site lists the lookout as removed (no date given)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Hood National Forest)

events.note: Forest Service set up a tent and alidade platform (firetower.org); firelookout.com lists a platform and camp; the Oregon site notes an alidade established
Panorama photos taken July 10, 1930 (Oregon lookout history site)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as US 634 on September 19, 2010

evidence.supports: 1913 tent and alidade platform, now gone
evidence.quote: In 1913 the USFS set up a tent and alidade platform, which is now gone.

evidence.supports: location: 20 miles northwest of Mt. Hood

evidence.quote: July 10, 1930: Panorama photos taken by O.E.T.

evidence.supports: panoramic view dated 1933 and credited to the National Archives
evidence.quote: Palmer Peak Lookout panoramic 7-11-33 - courtesy of National Archives-Pacific Northwest Region
1946: The lookout listed as an emergency lookout.

evidence.supports: U.S. Forest Service administers the site

sources.title: Palmer Peak
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Oregon), Rex's Fire Lookout Page

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree the 1913 platform is gone, but none gives a removal date or says what remains today; access is unknown. Oregon has a second Palmer Peak (Crater/Rogue River NF, Jackson County, 1914 lookout per Medford Mail Tribune items on oregonlookouts.weebly.com/palmer-peak1.html); it is a different site and was excluded. The 1930 and 1933 panorama dates are for two photos, not a conflict. The USGS page search hit was Joel Palmer's journal, not used. The brief's FFLOS registration date (September 19, 2010) matches firetower.org.
